La Once Mil - Roma Norte.note: Michelin's star is for the Lomas location

Siembra Taqueria.note: Listed by Michelin as Siembra Tortillería

additions.name: El Vilsito
additions.vibe: Late-night taquería set inside a working auto shop: trompo-spun al pastor and cheesy gringas under fluorescent lights.

additions.name: Los Cocuyos
additions.vibe: A taquero with a cleaver working a bubbling cauldron of meat since 1980. Order the cabeza or the al pastor.

additions.name: La 89
additions.vibe: Tiny Roma Norte taco nook grilling carne asada and quesabirria to order, on plastic stools with no frills.

additions.name: Los Consentidos del Barrio
additions.vibe: Upstairs charcoal grill serving thin-sliced tacos al carbón and a pink-centered arrachera.

additions.name: Tacos Charly
additions.vibe: Cash-only stand in Tlalpan known for confit-simmered suadero and carved al pastor. Get there early.

additions.name: Tacos del Valle (Roma Norte)
additions.vibe: Retro-diner taquería on Álvaro Obregón spinning pork and beef on the trompo, finished with squeeze-bottle salsas.

additions.name: Taquería El Jarocho
additions.vibe: Three generations deep in Roma Norte, serving guisado tacos out of a former tortillería. The pork flank in morita chile is the one.

additions.name: Taquería Los Milanesos
additions.vibe: Cash-only taco stand under an orange awning, piling on breaded pork cutlet.

additions.name: Torobi by Kazu Kumoto
additions.vibe: Chef Kazu Kumoto's Polanco spot where each table has its own built-in grill and you cook your own cuts from the best ingredients, at your own pace.

additions.name: Max
additions.vibe: A traditional tachinomi-style Japanese standing bar in Juárez for good food and strong drinks -- no chairs, open 5pm to close, Monday to Saturday.

additions.name: Itzu Prado Sur
additions.vibe: The Lomas-Virreyes branch of Itzu, serving sushi, ramen, bowls, and a rib-eye sukiyaki alongside its usual Japanese menu.

additions.name: Rekō Mx
additions.vibe: A new asian-fusion spot on Reforma -- order the tostadas, a lychee martini, and close with the chocolate cake.

additions.name: Tori
additions.vibe: Born in Japan, built for Mexico: a Polanco spot for rolls, nigiri, teppanyaki, and oysters.

additions.name: Maison Frite
additions.vibe: A Roma Norte spot devoted entirely to double-cooked French fries -- classic, goat cheese, or dressed up with house sauces.

additions.name: Café Tim
additions.vibe: A Santa María la Ribera café with good coffee and cooler-than-average merch, open Monday to Saturday.

additions.name: Tatsumi
additions.vibe: An intimate Lomas de Chapultepec sushi bar built entirely around its counter -- a self-described bridge between Mexico and Japan.

additions.name: Siembra Terraza
additions.vibe: From the Siembra family, a wide, warm-toned San Miguel Chapultepec terrace for breakfast, tacos, and corn-forward plates, or just drinks.

additions.name: Kari Kari
additions.vibe: A New-York-style temaki counter in Las Virreyes for fast, high-quality, everyday sushi.

additions.name: Chalino Chino Coyoacán
additions.vibe: The Coyoacán branch of the Sinaloa-style seafood spot with Asian touches that keeps expanding across the city.

additions.name: Fame Pizza
additions.vibe: CDMX's first Milano-style pizzeria, in Roma Norte -- tall, fried, and heavy on the cheese.

additions.name: Club Sándwich
additions.vibe: An unfussy Condesa sandwich shop open 8am to 10pm daily, doing simple things well.

additions.name: Myka Parque Duraznos
additions.vibe: A second CDMX location for the Greek frozen yogurt everyone's obsessed with, this one in Bosque de las Lomas.

additions.name: Café Cruda
additions.vibe: A Roma Norte café built around local, agroecological sourcing -- coffee, natural wine, and bread to go.

additions.name: Taller de Grassa
additions.vibe: The Condesa spot that gave smash burgers a proper home, open Wednesday to Sunday from 2pm.

additions.name: Payna
additions.vibe: Fresh-forward Roma Norte seafood -- oysters, tacos, tostadas -- from a new Mexico City marisco spot.

additions.name: Crumbl
additions.vibe: The viral pink-box cookie chain's first Mexico City spot, in Roma Norte, with a rotating weekly lineup alongside the classic chocolate chip.
